Adamsville — shaped ground + fresh water▾

Stage-2 shaping: the ground now carries your rulings. Every building lot is levelled to a pad — 24,407 buildings; look for the flat benches in the shading. Creeks keep the channels nature cut; where a road or rail bed dammed a drainage, the flow is carved through (151 dams opened) — never filled, never ponded.

Built at your ruled mix: fine 2 m ground near roads and houses, 10 m elsewhere; this preview's mesh is drawn 8 m near / 30 m far, sampled from the Stage-2 package's own grids. Ground runs 730 ft (Chattahoochee) to 1,123 ft. Vertical scale is TRUE (1.0) unless you change it below. Still terrain only — no roads or houses yet; those are the next steps.

The water was rebuilt fresh. The old map's water list was thrown out — it drew lakes where no lake is. Every blue fill here earned its place: 22 ponds and lakes confirmed by eye on Google satellite, Tatum Lake at its surveyed level (822.5 ft), and Wildwood Lake (813.5 ft), which the ground data measures directly. Each level comes from the water's own measured surface in the ground data — never from the old list — and every bed is cut 0.6 m below its level.

What you do NOT see is the point. 277 checked sites that Google showed were dry — mostly road and rail embankments fooling the ground scan — are excluded. One canopy-hidden site stays unresolved and undrawn, and no unchecked candidate is drawn either. No invented water.

The Chattahoochee itself is drawn along its real course at the zone's NW edge, at its own levels — about 740–743 ft where it leaves the zone — water only where the ground truly falls to it.
